diagnostic_methods: When alarms go to insufficient-data rather than firing, treat that as a signal in itself
Compare internal telemetry against external probes; divergence indicates the telemetry is affected
Work from logs when real-time telemetry is impaired, as AWS describes doing

evidence.citation: AWS, us-east-1 event December 7 2021
Datadog, deep dive into incident response for the 2023-03-08 incident
Brevo — status page hosted on the expired domain

incidents.summary: Congestion immediately impacted real-time monitoring data for internal operations teams, impairing their ability to find and resolve the source. Operators worked from logs and initially misread internal DNS errors as the primary problem. The Service Health Dashboard required manual updates for about 50 minutes and support-case creation was unavailable for around seven hours. Remediations include rebuilding the dashboard and restructuring support systems across multiple regions.

Datadog's own Datadog-based monitoring was largely unavailable during the incident. Detection came instead from basic out-of-band monitoring running completely outside their infrastructure, consuming their own public APIs like an external customer.
Dashboards and alerting depended on the Transit Gateways that failed. Slack's stated remediation is to move the dashboard service into the same VPC as its databases, removing the dependency.

leading_indicators.signal: Dependency audit of the telemetry, status and support paths against the systems they cover
Out-of-band probe results diverging from internal telemetry

observable_symptoms: Alarms transitioning to an insufficient-data state rather than firing
Dashboards stale or unavailable during the incident
Status page down or updated manually
Customers unable to open support cases
preconditions: Telemetry transiting the same network or platform it monitors
Status page hosted on the affected domain, DNS provider or region
Support case creation dependent on the affected service

known_limits: Requires a complete dependency graph for the telemetry path
Out-of-band monitoring trades fidelity for independence and cannot fully substitute
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Whether a signal shares a failure domain with what it monitors is a structural property, determinable in advance and recordable per signal.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: The telemetry, alerting, status page and support systems depend on the infrastructure they observe, so they degrade exactly when they are needed. The operational consequence is not just inconvenience: responders work from stale or absent data and misdiagnose. AWS states this directly for the December 2021 event — congestion immediately impacted the availability of real-time monitoring data for internal operations teams, which impaired their ability to find the source of congestion and resolve it.

remediations.action: Fall back to out-of-band monitoring and to logs
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Out-of-band monitoring is coarse and can support a wrong hypothesis
preconditions: Out-of-band monitoring exists
remediations.verification: Responders have a usable signal

remediations.action: Move telemetry, status and support paths off the shared dependency
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Not an incident-time action
preconditions: Design change
remediations.verification: Telemetry and status remain available with the production path deliberately severed

required_telemetry.signal: External synthetic probes running entirely outside the monitored infrastructure
Telemetry pipeline lag and drop counts

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Alarms entering insufficient-data state, or internal and external views diverging

root_causes: Consolidation of monitoring onto production infrastructure for cost or convenience
Status page sharing the production domain or DNS
Alarm evaluation dependent on the data path that failed
patterns.title: Monitoring, status and support channels inside the blast radius
verification: Verify recovery from the external vantage point first; internal telemetry recovering last is expected
Reconcile what the internal telemetry missed during the window, since gaps distort later analysis

affected_systems: any component behind a binary health check
automation_safety_limits: Health-check-driven eviction can cause a downward spiral under load: removing degraded capacity increases load on survivors, causing further evictions
Binary liveness checks cannot see this class at all, so automation built on them is blind by construction
diagnostic_methods: Compare peers doing identical work; the outlier is the finding, and absolute thresholds will not reveal it
Instrument the application's view of the dependency, not only the dependency's self-report
Expect long detection latency — Gunawi et al. report 1% of cases detected in minutes and 17% in months

evidence.citation: Gunawi et al., Fail-Slow at Scale, FAST '18
Huang et al., Gray Failure: The Achilles' Heel of Cloud-Scale Systems, HotOS '17

incidents.organisation: Gunawi et al. (FAST '18), reports from 12 institutions
incidents.summary: 101 fail-slow hardware reports. Documented cascade: a NIC degrading from 1 Gbps to 1 Kbps in one machine slowed an entire 100-machine cluster; a single bad disk exhausted a RAID card's performance. Degradation magnitudes include disk throughput falling to 100 KB/s due to vibration and CPUs running at 50% speed due to lack of power. The authors recommend online diagnosis and full-stack monitoring including fans, cables and power supplies.

Azure examples include a VM NIC driver defect invisible to a detector that never exercised the VM's external network, and a resource-reporting defect driving crash-reboot cycles that cascaded. The authors attribute most cloud incidents to gray failure based on first-hand experience, explicitly without a measured percentage — this is an experience claim in a workshop paper and should not be cited as a statistic.

leading_indicators.signal: Per-component latency percentile compared against peers performing identical work
Application-side observation of dependency health, as opposed to the dependency's self-report

observable_symptoms: Cluster-wide slowdown with every component reporting healthy
Tail latency degradation without error rate change
One component consistently slower than its peers
preconditions: Health checks that test liveness rather than performance
Work distribution that waits on the slowest participant
No peer comparison across nominally identical components

known_limits: Requires genuinely comparable peers doing comparable work
Detection latency is empirically poor: 1% in minutes, 17% in months
Does not distinguish internal defect from external cause without environmental telemetry
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Peer-relative outlier detection gives useful lead time — the degradation is gradual — but there is no published method for predicting which component will begin degrading.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: A component degrades rather than failing. Huang et al. define the condition as differential observability: the application observes the system as unhealthy while the failure detector observes it as healthy. The entity responsible for recovery is precisely the one that cannot see the fault. Gunawi et al.'s fail-slow study provides the hardware substrate — 101 reports across 12 institutions, with degradation both internal (firmware, wear) and external (temperature, power, configuration), and a documented tendency to propagate, because healthy nodes wait on the slow one.

remediations.action: Remove the degraded component from service
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Removing components on a false outlier signal reduces capacity and, under load, can start a downward spiral
preconditions: Peer comparison identifies the outlier reliably; a minimum-capacity floor is enforced
remediations.verification: Cluster latency percentiles recover after removal

remediations.action: Address the external cause — thermal, power, configuration
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Replacing hardware that was slowed by environment does not fix it — 39% of cases had external root causes
preconditions: Environmental telemetry available
remediations.verification: Performance returns to peer-normal without component replacement

required_telemetry.signal: Per-device and per-node latency percentiles for comparable operations
Application-side dependency latency and error observations
Environmental telemetry — temperature, power, fan state

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: A component persistently in the latency outlier position relative to identical peers

root_causes: Device wear, firmware defects, thermal or power conditions
Configuration inducing hardware-level slowness
Health checks that do not exercise the path the application uses
patterns.title: Gray failure and fail-slow degradation
verification: Confirm latency percentiles across the cluster, not only on the removed component
Confirm the cause was internal before replacing hardware

affected_systems: any alerting built on specific event shapes
automation_safety_limits: Automated detection cannot flag its own blind spots; coverage must be established by deliberate exercise
Absence of alerts is not evidence of absence of activity, and automation that assumes otherwise is unsafe
diagnostic_methods: Enumerate every path to the sensitive outcome and test each one against live detection
Search audit logs for event types that no rule references
Treat externally-reported incidents as evidence of a coverage gap, not only of an attack

evidence.citation: Okta, Root cause of unauthorized access to the support case management system

incidents.summary: A compromised service account was used to access the support case system for about 19 days. Okta initially missed the file downloads because the attacker used the Files tab directly, generating log events the team's detection logic did not recognise. The compromise surfaced only from a customer-supplied IP indicator. 134 customers affected; five had sessions hijacked.

leading_indicators.signal: Coverage test — for each access path to a sensitive outcome, does a detection rule fire?
Event shapes present in audit logs that match no detection rule

observable_symptoms: Activity discovered by an external party rather than internal detection
Audit logs containing the activity but no alert having fired
A long interval between the activity and its discovery
preconditions: Detection rules keyed to specific event shapes rather than to outcomes
Multiple access paths producing different events for the same effect
No coverage test asserting that each path produces a detectable event

known_limits: Requires a complete enumeration of access paths, which is the hard part
New application features silently add paths and therefore silently reduce coverage
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Coverage is a deterministic property: enumerate paths, exercise each, confirm an alert. It requires no model and yields an exact answer.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: A system emits events for an action, and the detection rules match one shape of those events. A different but equally legitimate access path produces events of a different shape, which the rules do not recognise. Nothing is missing from the logs; the logs simply do not say what the rules expect. The blind spot is invisible because the absence of alerts is indistinguishable from the absence of activity.

remediations.action: Extend detection to cover the unrecognised event shape
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: A rule written too broadly produces noise and is later disabled, recreating the gap
preconditions: The path and its event shape are understood
remediations.verification: A synthetic exercise of that path produces an alert

remediations.action: Bind sessions to additional context to limit the value of a stolen token
remediations.blast_radius: Session handling for the bound population
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Overly strict binding locks out legitimate users who change network context
preconditions: Clients tolerate the additional binding
remediations.verification: A token replayed from a different context is rejected

required_telemetry.signal: Full audit event stream, independent of which rules consume it
Detection-rule coverage mapping paths to rules

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Any sensitive activity discovered by an external party
rollback_and_escalation.rollback_notes: Access that already occurred cannot be undone; only the gap can be closed

root_causes: Rules written against the access path that was known at the time
New or less-common access paths added without updating detection
Coverage assessed by rule count rather than by path enumeration
patterns.title: Detection-logic blind spot — a legitimate path that emits no recognised event
verification: Verify by exercising each path and confirming an alert, not by reviewing rule definitions
Re-verify after any change to the application's access paths

affected_systems: any system operated by humans under time pressure
automation_safety_limits: Automation reduces routine toil but, per Google SRE, creates skill atrophy: automation fails and the humans are now unable to operate the system, because the manual path no longer exists
The countermeasure documented in Building Secure and Reliable Systems is to make the emergency path the everyday path turned up to maximum, and to enforce break-glass exercise intervals
diagnostic_methods: In post-incident analysis, check responder count and hours worked as a contributing factor, not as blame
Check whether the recovery step that failed had ever been performed before

evidence.citation: GitLab.com database incident
Google SRE, Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure
Google SRE, The Evolution of Automation at Google — skill atrophy

incidents.summary: An engineer working late on a replication problem ran a deletion command against the production cluster rather than the secondary. GitLab's postmortem records that the engineer had said they were signing off around 23:00 local time but continued working through the incident. ~18 hours of downtime and roughly six hours of lost records.

The overnight crew at the data centre lacked the electrical expertise needed, and access-control systems had lost power. Cloudflare had tested partial facility failures but never a full facility shutdown.
Recovery was prolonged because the affected configuration was undocumented and the restore runbook was untested.

leading_indicators.signal: Incident duration and responder count — a long incident with one responder is the risk condition
Time since the relevant runbook was last exercised

observable_symptoms: A second, larger incident occurring during remediation of the first
Recovery time dominated by figuring out how things work rather than by doing anything
Runbook steps that do not match reality
preconditions: Single responder on a long-running incident outside normal hours
Destructive commands executable directly against production
Recovery procedures not exercised

known_limits: Detecting the condition is easy; the intervention is organisational and cannot be automated
Fatigue is not directly measurable, only inferred from hours and time of day
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Incident duration, responder count, local time and runbook staleness are all directly observable. The risk condition is computable in real time during an incident.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: A long incident, worked late and alone, produces a second and worse incident. The mechanism is not mysterious: tired people operating directly on production with similar-looking target names make target-selection errors, and there is no second person to catch them. A closely related process failure is discovering during recovery that the runbook is wrong, undocumented or has never been exercised — which converts a technical problem into an archaeology problem.

remediations.action: Enforce handover and a second responder on long incidents
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Handover itself loses context if not structured
preconditions: Enough responders exist to rotate
remediations.verification: Handover occurred and the incoming responder has context

remediations.action: Require a second pair of eyes for destructive production commands
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: An unreachable reviewer blocks a genuinely urgent action; a break-glass path is required
preconditions: A reviewer is reachable at the time
remediations.verification: Destructive operations carry an approval record

remediations.action: Rehearse recovery procedures on a schedule
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: A rehearsal that touches production creates the incident it was meant to prevent
preconditions: An isolated environment; the rehearsal cannot touch production
remediations.verification: The rehearsal itself is the verification

required_telemetry.signal: Incident duration, responder count and local time per responder
Runbook last-exercised dates

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Incident exceeding a defined duration with a single responder

root_causes: No enforced handover on long incidents
Production and non-production targets distinguishable only by a character
Runbooks written once and never rehearsed
patterns.title: Fatigue, solo working and untested recovery procedure
verification: Post-incident analysis should be blameless: Google SRE defines this as identifying contributing causes without indicting any individual or team, and requires review — an unreviewed postmortem might as well never have existed
Verify that action items from the analysis are actually completed, which this research could not find published data on

affected_systems: horizontally autoscaled services, particularly I/O-bound ones
automation_safety_limits: Autoscaling must be disabled or floored during declared incidents; this is the cheapest available guardrail
The scale-up path must be load-tested, or the recovery automation fails at the moment it is needed
Emergency capacity requests are bounded by cloud quotas that must be raised in advance
diagnostic_methods: Check whether CPU and latency moved in opposite directions; this is the inversion signature
Review scaling events against the incident timeline before assuming the autoscaler was passive

evidence.citation: Slack's Outage on January 4th 2021
Tom Wilkie, The RED Method — RED deliberately omits saturation
Kubernetes HPA documentation — stabilisation window and scaling behaviour policies

incidents.summary: Network problems meant threads spent more time waiting, which caused CPU utilisation to drop, and that drop initially triggered automated downscaling. Slack subsequently attempted to add 1,200 servers in 14 minutes, at which point provision-service hit the Linux open-files limit and an AWS quota. Remediations include re-evaluating autoscaling configuration so it cannot overload provision-service.

leading_indicators.signal: Divergence between CPU utilisation and request latency (falling CPU with rising latency)
Replica-count oscillation, indicating thrash

observable_symptoms: Capacity shrinking while error rates rise
CPU falling while latency rises — the inversion signature
Scale-up attempts later failing on their own resource limits
preconditions: Scaling policy keyed to CPU utilisation on an I/O-bound workload
No floor on scale-down during degraded conditions
No stabilisation window or asymmetric scale-down policy

known_limits: Requires both signals to be collected and compared, which many scaling configurations do not do
Does not cover other proxy inversions that have not yet been characterised
predictive_monitoring.rationale: The inversion is a two-signal comparison with an unambiguous signature. Detecting "CPU down, latency up" requires a rule, not a model.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: Autoscaling uses a proxy for demand. During certain failures the proxy inverts: when threads block on a slow dependency they consume less CPU, so an I/O-bound service under network distress looks idle. The autoscaler then removes capacity precisely when capacity is needed. Slack's account is explicit — network problems meant threads spent more time waiting, CPU utilisation dropped, and that drop triggered automated downscaling.

remediations.action: Disable scale-down for the duration of the incident
remediations.blast_radius: Capacity is preserved at current levels; cost increases
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Preserving capacity during a genuine demand drop wastes money but is rarely harmful
preconditions: Error rate or latency threshold breached
remediations.verification: Replica count stops falling

remediations.action: Scale on a signal that does not invert — queue depth, latency or in-flight requests
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Latency-based scaling can amplify a dependency problem by adding load to it
preconditions: The signal is available and stable
remediations.verification: Injected dependency slowness produces scale-up, not scale-down

remediations.action: Apply stabilisation windows and asymmetric scale-down policies
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Over-damping makes the autoscaler too slow for genuine demand spikes
preconditions: Autoscaler supports the controls
remediations.verification: Replica count no longer oscillates under noisy load

required_telemetry.signal: CPU utilisation and request latency together
Replica count over time and scaling events
Thread state distribution — running versus blocked

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Replica count falling while error rate or latency rises

root_causes: CPU used as a saturation proxy for an I/O-bound service — precisely the gap the RED method's authors identify, since RED deliberately omits saturation
No guard preventing scale-down during elevated error rates
Reactive scaling on noisy instantaneous metrics
patterns.title: Autoscaler acting on a proxy signal that inverts during an incident
verification: Verify by injecting dependency slowness and confirming the autoscaler does not remove capacity
Load-test the scale-up path itself, since it failed on its own limits during recovery

automation_safety_limits: This is the meta-pattern for the whole automation-safety family: every guardrail in the catalog is subject to it
Safety automation needs its own testing — Meta's audit tool that should have blocked the October 2021 command had a bug
diagnostic_methods: Deliberately fail the gate and confirm the action is blocked; reading the code is insufficient
Audit for deployments that proceeded without a positive verdict

evidence.citation: Google Compute Engine incident 16007
SEC Administrative Proceeding 34-70694 (Knight Capital)

incidents.summary: Two compounding automation defects. On detecting configuration inconsistency, the management software removed all GCE IP blocks instead of retaining the previous known-good configuration — fail-open-to-empty rather than fail-safe. Separately, a second defect meant the canary step's conclusion was not propagated back to the push process. Result: 18 minutes with over 95% loss of inbound internet traffic to all GCE instances globally. Remediations included comparing IP block announcements before and after changes and adding semantic checks that configurations contain expected blocks.

The detection-without-enforcement pattern in its starkest form: pre-deployment warning messages were generated and never read, because Knight did not design those messages to be system alerts, and there was no mechanism to halt the system in response to its own aberrant activity.

leading_indicators.signal: Verdict-to-action linkage test — does a deliberately failing gate actually block?
Rate of actions proceeding despite a negative gate verdict

observable_symptoms: A bad change reaching production despite a gate reporting failure
Gate logs showing the correct verdict and the action proceeding anyway
Fail-open behaviour in a path that should fail closed
preconditions: Detection and enforcement implemented as separate components
No fail-closed behaviour when the verdict cannot be obtained
Safety-path code not itself tested for failure

known_limits: Requires a safe way to fail the gate deliberately
Proves the linkage worked at test time, not that it works under every failure mode of the gate
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Whether a gate actually blocks is testable at any time by deliberately failing it. The answer is exact and requires no production incident to obtain.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: The safety gate detects the problem and the detection does not stop the action. In Google Compute Engine incident 16007 the canary step correctly identified a bad configuration, but a second defect in the management software did not propagate the canary's conclusion back to the push process, so the push proceeded. The lesson generalises beyond canaries: a detector without an enforced veto path is decorative.

remediations.action: Make the gate blocking and fail closed when the verdict is unavailable
remediations.blast_radius: Deployments block when the gate is unavailable
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: A gate that fails closed and is itself unreliable blocks all deployments, including emergency fixes
preconditions: A break-glass override exists for genuine emergencies
remediations.verification: A deliberately failing gate blocks the action

remediations.action: Preserve last known good rather than emptying on inconsistency
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Retaining a stale configuration indefinitely can be its own failure
preconditions: A known-good state is retained and validated
remediations.verification: Injected inconsistency results in retention, not removal

required_telemetry.signal: Gate verdicts paired with the resulting action outcome
Count of deployments proceeding with a failing or missing verdict

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Any action proceeding with a negative or absent gate verdict

root_causes: Verdict propagation implemented as a best-effort notification
Gate treated as advisory rather than blocking
The safety path never exercised with a genuine failure
patterns.title: Canary correct but not enforced
verification: Verify by exercise: fail the gate deliberately and confirm the block
Verify periodically, since the linkage can regress silently like any other untested path

affected_systems: any predict-and-act loop — failure prediction, capacity prediction, anomaly-driven remediation
automation_safety_limits: This is the structural argument against fully closed-loop prediction without a control arm — A4 automation requires one
A model that has silently degraded will keep acting confidently; degradation is invisible without the control arm
diagnostic_methods: Compare model performance on treated and untreated populations; if there is no untreated population, the measurement cannot be made
Check whether performance degrades monotonically across retraining cycles

evidence.citation: Li et al., Why does Prediction Accuracy Decrease over Time? Uncertain Positive Learning for Cloud Failure Prediction
Levy et al., Narya: Predictive and Adaptive Failure Mitigation, OSDI '20

incidents.summary: Deployed failure predictors degrade measurably over time. The stated mechanism is that mitigation alters the original state, rendering it unverifiable whether the failure would have occurred. Microsoft reports that in real-world practice prediction accuracy may decrease by about 9% after retraining the models. Dataset scale includes over 500,000 node recordings on Azure, over 90,000 disks on Backblaze, and millions of disks over 16+ months on Alibaba.

The countermeasure in practice: Narya's action set includes an explicit NoOp control arm alongside live migration, soft reboot, mark-unallocatable and service healing. Reported performance is precision 79.49%, recall 50.7%, false-positive rate 20.51%, median lead time 2.44 days, with a 26% reduction in VM interruptions against an achievable ceiling of 35.4%.

leading_indicators.signal: Model performance measured on a held-out untreated control population
Proportion of positive predictions that received an action, and are therefore unlabelled

observable_symptoms: Model precision and recall declining over successive periods with no change in the system
Retraining making performance worse rather than better
Increasing divergence between predicted and observed failure rates
preconditions: A model whose positive predictions trigger an action
Labels derived from observed outcomes after the action
No untreated control arm

known_limits: Requires deliberately withholding mitigation from some population, which has a real cost
Control-arm sizing is a statistical-power question that this research did not find addressed in the literature
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Given a control arm, the degradation is directly measurable. Without one, it is not measurable at all — which is the point.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: A predictive model triggers a mitigation. The mitigation prevents the predicted failure, so it becomes unverifiable whether the failure would have occurred. Labels derived from these outcomes are therefore corrupt, and retraining on them degrades the model further. This is not ordinary concept drift; it is a structural consequence of acting on predictions, and it is measured: Microsoft reports Azure performance decreasing from 78.22% at one period to 57.46% at a later one, with Backblaze and Alibaba showing decreases of 8.34% and 13.77%.

remediations.action: Maintain a held-out untreated control arm
remediations.blast_radius: A defined fraction of predicted failures go unmitigated
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: The control arm suffers real failures that could have been prevented — this is a genuine, deliberate cost
preconditions: The cost of not acting on the control arm is acceptable
remediations.verification: Model performance measurable on the control arm over time

remediations.action: Record prediction, action and outcome as separate fields rather than collapsing them
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Without this, no later analysis can recover the distinction
preconditions: Data model supports it
remediations.verification: Treated and untreated outcomes are distinguishable in the data

remediations.action: Prefer cheap, reversible actions so a high false-positive rate is affordable
remediations.blast_radius: Bounded by the action's own cost
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Cheap actions may not actually prevent the failure, giving false confidence
preconditions: Cheap actions exist that address the predicted failure
remediations.verification: Measured outcome improvement against the prior static strategy

required_telemetry.signal: Prediction, action taken, and observed outcome recorded as separate fields
Control-arm assignment and its outcomes

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Model performance declining across successive evaluation periods
rollback_and_escalation.rollback_notes: Reverting to a prior model version is possible, but the label corruption persists in the data

root_causes: Acting on every positive prediction, leaving no counterfactual
Treating post-mitigation non-failure as a negative label
Retraining on contaminated labels
patterns.title: Predictor self-poisoning — remediation destroys the ground truth
verification: Verify model performance against the control arm, never against treated outcomes
Verify that retraining improves rather than degrades performance before adopting a new model

automation_safety_limits: Eviction throttles in the Kubernetes Descheduler are optional and unenforced if unset — availability of a guardrail is not the same as its being in effect
Remediation systems must treat "many nodes unhealthy at once" as evidence of a systemic cause, not as many independent faults
Health-check-driven eviction under load can produce a downward spiral, as noted in F9.2
diagnostic_methods: Compare the fault-declaration rate against baseline; a correlated cause produces an anomalous rate
Check whether the nodes entering remediation share a version, image or configuration
Verify whether concurrency caps are actually configured, since several tools leave them optional

evidence.citation: Microsoft, Summary of Windows Azure service disruption on Feb 29th, 2012
Medik8s Node Healthcheck Operator configuration — minHealthy/maxUnhealthy mandatory, stormCooldownDuration
GKE node auto-repair documentation — adaptive parallelism
Kubernetes Descheduler README — eviction limits are optional and unenforced if unset

incidents.summary: Three consecutive agent-handshake timeouts on a clean VM caused the host agent to conclude a hardware fault and report the server, which was then service-healed onto another server where the same date bug reproduced — converting a software defect into a spreading hardware-failure declaration across the fleet.

leading_indicators.signal: Count of nodes concurrently under remediation, against a configured maximum
Rate of fault declarations against historical baseline
Healthy-node count against a minimum floor

observable_symptoms: Many nodes entering remediation simultaneously
Available capacity falling while the remediation system reports normal operation
Quorum loss in a coordination cluster due to concurrent member remediation
preconditions: Per-node remediation triggers with no fleet-level constraint
A fault condition that is correlated across nodes rather than isolated
Remediation that removes capacity (drain, reboot, recreate)

known_limits: Requires the caps to be configured; defaults in several tools are permissive or absent
Does not by itself distinguish a correlated software cause from genuine mass hardware failure
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Concurrent remediation count against a cap, and fault-declaration rate against baseline, are both direct measurements with unambiguous thresholds.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: A condition affects many nodes at once. The remediation system, designed for isolated failures, attempts to repair all of them concurrently — draining, rebooting or recreating so much of the fleet that capacity collapses or quorum is lost. The mechanism is that the remediation policy has a per-node trigger and no fleet-level floor. The Azure leap-day incident is the documented case of a software fault being laundered into mass hardware-fault verdicts and mass relocation.

remediations.action: Enforce a quorum guard and storm cooldown on mass remediation
remediations.blast_radius: Remediation pauses when the fleet is broadly unhealthy
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: A guard set too tight prevents remediation of genuine widespread hardware failure
preconditions: A minimum-healthy or maximum-unhealthy value is configured — Medik8s makes one of these mandatory with no default
remediations.verification: Injected mass unhealthiness does not trigger mass remediation

remediations.action: Halt the remediation system entirely
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Genuine failures accumulate unrepaired
preconditions: Manual remediation is feasible for the duration
remediations.verification: Concurrent remediation count returns to zero

remediations.action: Scale remediation parallelism with fleet size and inversely with unhealthy count
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Adaptive policy tuned wrongly either storms or stalls
preconditions: Remediation system supports adaptive parallelism — GKE documents repairing more nodes in parallel on larger clusters but fewer as unhealthy count grows
remediations.verification: Parallelism falls as unhealthy count rises

required_telemetry.signal: Concurrent remediation count and per-node remediation state
Healthy versus unhealthy node counts
Fault-declaration rate per hour

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Concurrent remediation count above the configured maximum, or fault-declaration rate far above baseline

root_causes: Remediation policy without a quorum guard or storm cooldown
Fault classification that cannot distinguish a correlated software cause from independent hardware faults
Eviction throttles left at their defaults, which in some tools are optional and unenforced if unset
patterns.title: Remediation storm — mass automated repair outrunning the fleet's capacity to absorb it
verification: Confirm healthy capacity is recovering, not just that remediations are completing
Confirm the concurrency guard is configured, not merely available

automation_safety_limits: Automated failover must be aware of environmental correlation; two providers in the same city share weather
Automated rebuild of redundancy must be rate-limited against infrastructure that has just recovered
No automation shortens a repair bounded by ship scheduling or parts logistics
diagnostic_methods: Check facility telemetry before investigating software causes when a whole zone degrades
After recovery, explicitly enumerate resources left in reduced redundancy

evidence.citation: Google Cloud incident, europe-west2 cooling, July 2022
Cloudflare, Post-mortem on control plane and analytics outage
Internet Society, 2024 West Africa Submarine Cable Outage Report

incidents.summary: A cooling-related failure in a building hosting europe-west2-a during the UK heatwave. Partial capacity failure in the zone, VM terminations and machine loss for a small set of customers. Some replicated Persistent Disk devices ran in single-redundancy mode and HDD-backed volumes saw IO errors. Parts of the zone were powered down to prevent further damage; restoring redundancy was a separate listed remediation.

Unplanned utility maintenance switched the facility to generators without notifying Cloudflare; roughly three hours later a ground fault took down both utility feeds and the generators simultaneously. UPS batteries lasted a fraction of their design duration.

A suspected underwater rock slide off the coast of Côte d'Ivoire severed four submarine cables, degrading connectivity across 13 countries. Repairs ran from late March to mid-May — roughly six weeks — bounded by repair-ship availability and sea state rather than by engineering effort.

leading_indicators.signal: Facility environmental telemetry — temperature, power feed state, generator readiness
Count of resources currently in reduced-redundancy state
Concentration of capacity within one environmental risk zone

observable_symptoms: Loss of a zone or building, with VM terminations and machine loss
Replicated storage running in reduced redundancy after the event
Repair timelines measured in weeks for physical transport failures
preconditions: Capacity concentrated in one facility or one environmental risk zone
Redundancy that was consumed by the incident and not yet restored
Physical repair paths with long lead times

known_limits: Facility telemetry is inside the blast radius of a power event
Weather correlation requires external data that most capacity models do not incorporate
Repair timelines are set by third parties and are not forecastable internally
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Environmental telemetry gives minutes to hours of warning for thermal events, and reduced-redundancy state is a deterministic inventory question. The physical event itself is not predictable from the systems' own telemetry.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: Physical infrastructure fails, and the failure is correlated across everything in the building or the weather system. Two properties distinguish this family from software failure. First, recovery time is bounded by logistics — repair crews, ship schedules, parts — not by engineering. Second, the visible incident can close while the system remains in a degraded redundancy state that is a second incident waiting.

remediations.action: Shed capacity deliberately to prevent physical damage
remediations.blast_radius: Part of a zone taken offline
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Shedding capacity unnecessarily causes an avoidable customer outage
preconditions: Environmental telemetry indicates a damage threshold
remediations.verification: Temperature or power state returns to safe range

remediations.action: Restore redundancy for resources left in a reduced state
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: An unthrottled mass rebuild can saturate the infrastructure that just recovered
preconditions: Capacity available; rebuild rate limited to avoid saturating the recovered infrastructure
remediations.verification: Every affected resource confirmed back at full redundancy

remediations.action: Shift workload to another zone
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Moving into a zone affected by the same weather system achieves nothing
preconditions: Target zone has capacity and is not in the same environmental risk zone
remediations.verification: Workload healthy in the new zone

required_telemetry.signal: Per-facility power and cooling state
Storage redundancy state per volume
Diverse-path inventory for network transport

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Any resource remaining in reduced redundancy after the visible incident closes

root_causes: Cooling failure under extreme ambient temperature
Utility fault taking both feeds and generators together
Physical cable damage from environmental events
patterns.title: Power, cooling and physical-environment failure, with residual degraded redundancy
verification: Explicitly enumerate and close out reduced-redundancy resources; the status page turning green does not mean redundancy was restored
For transport failures, verify diverse-path restoration rather than aggregate connectivity

affected_systems: any model trained on ingested data
automation_safety_limits: Automated retraining pipelines will faithfully incorporate poisoned data; ingestion validation is the only automatable control
Availability-based automation is blind to this class entirely
diagnostic_methods: Compare output quality against the training-data timeline rather than against deployments
Trace lineage to identify which source contributed the degraded data
Expect the recovery path to be data rebuild and retraining, not rollback

evidence.citation: Unity Software Q1 2022 earnings call, management statements on training-data ingestion and Audience Pinpointer accuracy
evidence.publisher: The Motley Fool (transcript of first-party statements)

incidents.summary: Management stated a fault in the platform resulted in reduced accuracy for a targeting tool, and that the company lost the value of a portion of its training data due in part to ingesting bad data from a large customer. Estimated impact was roughly $110 million in 2022. The stated recovery path was data rebuilding, then model retraining, then revenue recovery as customers scaled spend back up — described as iterative.

leading_indicators.signal: Input data distribution compared against historical baseline, per source
Model output quality tracked as a service level, not just availability

observable_symptoms: Output quality degrading while availability and latency are normal
Business metrics declining ahead of any technical signal
Degradation persisting after the bad input stops
preconditions: Ingestion of external or customer-supplied data into a training path
No validation of input data distribution against expectation
Model quality not monitored as a first-class service level

known_limits: Distribution comparison catches gross shifts, not subtle poisoning
Output quality degradation may only be observable in business metrics with substantial lag
This research found no first-party postmortem of a named training-serving skew incident; F13 is the least-evidenced family
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Input distribution shift is detectable at ingestion, before training, by comparison against a historical baseline per source. This is a validation gate, not a model.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: Bad input data is ingested and used to train or update a model. The system stays available and its outputs stay plausible, so availability monitoring shows nothing — the failure is in output quality. Recovery is fundamentally different from a software incident: there is no rollback, because the remedy is rebuilding the data and retraining, which takes as long as it takes.

remediations.action: Stop ingesting from the implicated source
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Excluding a legitimate source degrades the model in a different way
preconditions: Source identified via lineage
remediations.verification: Input distribution returns to baseline

remediations.action: Rebuild the affected training data and retrain
remediations.blast_radius: Model quality during the rebuild period
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Retraining on partially-cleaned data extends the degradation
preconditions: Clean data can be reconstructed or reacquired
remediations.verification: Output quality measured against a held-out clean evaluation set

remediations.action: Roll back to a prior model version
remediations.blast_radius: Serving quality reverts to the older model
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: The prior model may be stale in other respects, trading one quality problem for another
preconditions: A prior model version is retained and still valid for current traffic
remediations.verification: Output quality improves on the evaluation set

required_telemetry.signal: Per-source input distribution statistics at ingestion
Model output quality metrics over time
Training-data provenance and lineage

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Output quality degrading while availability is normal
rollback_and_escalation.rollback_notes: Model rollback is possible; data corruption is not reversible and must be rebuilt

root_causes: Ingesting bad data from a single large source without validation
Treating data quality as an upstream concern rather than an operational one
No separation between data intended for training and data intended only for serving
patterns.title: Upstream data poisoning degrading a model or derived dataset
verification: Verify against a held-out clean evaluation set, not against production traffic that may itself be affected
Expect recovery to be gradual and measured in business outcomes rather than in technical metrics

affected_systems: automated decision systems with financial consequence
automation_safety_limits: This is the clearest case in the catalog for a hard exposure limit on any automated decision system, independent of model confidence
Model availability monitoring is entirely blind to this failure; the system works correctly throughout
Knight Capital's lesson generalises: an automated system acting on its own outputs needs a halt mechanism that does not depend on recognising that the outputs are wrong
diagnostic_methods: Measure interval calibration continuously — the fraction of realised outcomes outside the stated interval is the direct test
Track cumulative exposure independently of per-decision confidence

evidence.citation: Zillow Group Q3 2021 Shareholder Letter

incidents.summary: Zillow's Q3 2021 shareholder letter states they were unable to accurately forecast future home prices at different times in both directions by much more than they had modelled as possible. The result was a $304 million write-down on Q3 inventory from buying homes above later price estimates, with unit economics swinging roughly 1,200 basis points from the prior quarter. The failure is financial rather than an availability event, and there was no rollback.

leading_indicators.signal: Realised-versus-predicted calibration — the fraction of outcomes falling outside the stated interval
Cumulative exposure created by model-driven decisions against a defined limit

observable_symptoms: Realised outcomes falling outside the predicted interval far more often than the interval implies
Losses accumulating while every system reports healthy
Unit economics diverging from model expectations
preconditions: Model outputs drive irreversible commitments
Error bounds estimated from historical data that does not cover the current regime
No circuit breaker on cumulative exposure

known_limits: Requires the model to state an interval, not just a point estimate
Calibration measurement lags by however long it takes outcomes to be realised
Regime changes can invalidate calibration faster than it can be measured
predictive_monitoring.rationale: Interval calibration is a direct, continuous measurement. If realised outcomes fall outside the stated interval more often than the interval claims, the model's error bounds are wrong — and that is knowable before the losses accumulate.

patterns.problem_and_mechanism: A model's predictions are used to make commitments, and the model's error distribution turns out to be wider than assumed. The system functions perfectly: it serves predictions, availability is fine, and the loss accrues through correct execution of decisions based on wrong forecasts. There is no rollback, because the commitments were real. Zillow's own framing is that they were unable to accurately forecast future home prices at different times in both directions by much more than they had modelled as possible.

remediations.action: Halt model-driven commitments
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Halting a functioning business line on a false signal has its own large cost
preconditions: A halt mechanism exists — the Knight Capital lesson applies directly
remediations.verification: No new commitments created

remediations.action: Widen the operating margin to absorb the observed error
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: Widening margins on a mis-measured distribution either over- or under-corrects
preconditions: Realised error distribution measured, not assumed
remediations.verification: Realised outcomes fall inside the revised interval at the expected rate

remediations.action: Impose a cumulative exposure limit
remediations.blast_radius: Decisions stop when the limit is reached
remediations.failure_mode_if_wrong: A limit set too low forgoes legitimate business
preconditions: Exposure is measurable in near real time
remediations.verification: Exposure remains within the limit

required_telemetry.signal: Predicted value, stated interval, and realised outcome recorded per decision
Cumulative exposure from model-driven decisions

rollback_and_escalation.escalation_trigger: Realised outcomes falling outside the stated interval materially more often than the interval implies
rollback_and_escalation.rollback_notes: Commitments already made cannot be unmade; only future decisions can be changed

root_causes: Error bounds calibrated on a historical regime that no longer holds
Absence of a limit on aggregate exposure created by automated decisions
Confusing model availability with model correctness
patterns.title: Model error exceeding its own modelled bounds
verification: Verify by calibration measurement over a sustained period, not by re-examining the model
Verify that a halt mechanism exists and has been exercised
